primary_meaning: Satan/the Devil as the embodiment of evil, deception, and temptation
primary_basis: Revelation 12:9 (ancient serpent identified as the devil/Satan)

alternatives.meaning: Literal animal or natural creature without necessary demonic identification
basis: Absence of explicit Satan language in the Hebrew text of Genesis

alternatives.meaning: Symbol of wisdom, shrewdness, or prudent cunning (sometimes positive)
basis: Proverbs 30:18-19 (serpent on a rock as wonder)
Ancient Near Eastern associations of serpents with wisdom

alternatives.meaning: Typological prefiguration of Christ and salvation/healing (bronze serpent)
basis: John 3:14-15 (Son of Man lifted up like the serpent)

alternatives.meaning: Chaos monster or primordial force of disorder (linked to Leviathan/Rahab imagery)
Agent of enlightenment or liberator of knowledge (non-orthodox/Gnostic readings)
basis: Select modern esoteric or revisionist treatments

notes: In mainstream Christian teaching and traditional biblical interpretation the identification of the Genesis serpent with Satan is the long-settled dominant reading, reinforced by New Testament explicit equations. Alternative senses appear in specific textual contexts (bronze serpent, shrewdness sayings) or in critical/Gnostic scholarship, but do not displace the primary Satanic symbolism in Christian consensus.
